system.context: Orbit's new assistant model scored 18 of 25 (72 percent) on the internal support benchmark against 17 of 25 (68 percent) for the old one, and the team wanted to ship on the four-point gain. Twenty-five items cannot settle a four-point difference: the two models disagree on only five items, so a handful of lucky draws decides the sign. Shipping on the point estimate alone treats one item's worth of difference as evidence.
system.request: A worked Python example of one action: bootstrap_differences(old, new, resamples, seed). Pair the two per-item result lists with a strict zip, resample the items with replacement using a seeded random.Random, score both models on each resample, collect new accuracy minus old accuracy, and report the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles (nearest rank) of the 200 differences as a 95 percent interval; if the interval includes zero the gain is not established. The lesson leads with the complete solution over 25 inline results and its exact output, explains the Python construct by construct, traces the first four resamples, measures the ship-on-the-point-estimate decision against the interval, and offers one practice variation: the share of resamples in which the new model is better.
inputs: Two lists of 25 results written inline in solution.py as 1 (right) or 0 (wrong), paired by position: OLD with 17 right and NEW with 18 right; 15 items right for both, 2 only for the old model, 3 only for the new one, 5 wrong for both
RESAMPLES of 200 and SEED of 5 for random.Random; the practice adds EXPECTED_BETTER, the share of resamples above zero (119 of 200)
The percentile convention: nearest rank, position round(share / 100 * (count - 1)) on the sorted differences
outputs: bootstrap_differences returns a list of 200 floats, new accuracy minus old accuracy per resample; percentile reads the 2.5th and 97.5th: -0.12 and 0.2 for this input

python solution.py prints the two accuracies, the observed difference of +4.0 points, the resample count and seed, the interval -12.0 to +20.0 points, the verdict that the gain is not established, the rejected shortened list, and OK; python/fixtures/expected-output.txt holds that output byte for byte

python starter.py prints NOT OK and exits 1 as shipped; after the practice change it also prints the probability the new model is better (59.5% of resamples) and OK, as python/fixtures/expected-practice-output.txt records for practice_answer.py
constraints: Standard library only (random, sys); each lesson file runs alone in an empty directory with python -I -S; no sibling imports, fixtures, credentials, or network
The resampling is paired (both models scored on the same drawn items) and seeded (the same seed replays the same draws); the generator is a random.Random object, never the module-level functions
Unequal result lists raise ValueError through zip(strict=True), and zero resamples raise ValueError; the input lists are never modified

Ordinary Python only: lists, tuples, a for loop with an unused underscore variable, += totals, division, sorted, round, f-strings with percent, sign, and whole-number formats, a chained comparison, a conditional expression, try and except, and assert; random.Random and randrange are the concepts taught; no classes, regular expressions, or comprehensions in the lesson files
successCriteria: solution.py run alone exits 0 and its output equals expected-output.txt byte for byte: 68.0% and 72.0%, +4.0 points, 200 resamples with seed 5, an interval of -12.0 to +20.0 points, the not-established verdict, the rejected line, and OK

The same seed reproduces the interval (-0.12, 0.2) and seed 7 gives (-0.16, 0.24); every resample draws exactly 25 indices in range and scoring them by hand matches the recorded difference; the percentile helper returns the nearest rank on a known list with Python's round-half-to-even

starter.py run alone exits 1 with NOT OK and no traceback; practice_answer.py run alone exits 0 and matches expected-practice-output.txt; better_fraction equals 119/200 with the 36 zero differences not counted

The point estimate alone would ship while the interval includes zero; 1,000 resamples with the same seed still give -0.12 to 0.2; a constructed pair where the new model adds eight right answers gives an interval entirely above zero

checks.description: solution.py copied alone into an empty directory and run with python -I -S exits 0 with empty stderr and prints expected-output.txt byte for byte.

The same seed replays the same 200 differences and the interval (-0.12, 0.2); seed 7 gives a different interval (-0.16, 0.24).
Replaying the generator, every resample draws exactly 25 indices between 0 and 24, some items repeat, and scoring those indices by hand gives the recorded difference.
percentile returns the nearest rank of a sorted copy (0, 4, 9 for the 0th, 50th, and 97.5th of a ten-value list) and the positions 5 and 194 for 200 values.
The interval is a real range that brackets the observed +0.04 and includes zero.

With 1,000 resamples and the same seed the interval is still -0.12 to 0.2 and includes zero.
For a constructed pair where the new model is right on everything the old one got right plus eight more items, the whole interval sits above zero.

practice_answer.py run alone exits 0 and prints expected-practice-output.txt byte for byte.

visuals.description: A short animation of the worked example, about two and a half seconds per shown resample and under half a minute in all: the 25 items as split squares (old and new, right or wrong), the first four resamples laid out one at a time as 25 tiles with repeats and scored (-8.0, +4.0, +8.0, +12.0 points), eight more resamples passing quickly, the remaining 188 filling the histogram of differences as a counter, the zero line and the 95% interval bracket (-12.0 to +20.0 points) with the not-established verdict, and the practice variation shading the 119 of 200 resamples above zero. Step buttons, pause, restart; the site's motion preference sets the pace and the two-minute rest between repeats; the still setting paints the finished state once.
visuals.correctness: The animation is driven by visuals/bootstrapModel.js, which rescores the shown resamples from the indices the Python file drew (python/fixtures/expected-trace.json), recomputes the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles with a round-half-to-even port of the solution's percentile rule, and recomputes the better share from the 200 Python differences; tests/benchmark-bootstrap-interval-viz.test.mjs asserts that result deep-equals expected-trace.json, which the cited Python check derives from the real solution. Python's seeded generator itself is not replayed in the browser, and the figure's counter says the remaining resamples are computed by the Python file. The test also checks the pace (each shown resample 2.4 to 3 seconds, the run 25 to 45 seconds), that the histogram total never exceeds the resamples completed, that the drawn tiles match the shown resample, and that the final scene shows the interval and the 119 above zero. Rendered frames were inspected at several moments.
